<!-- pr-reviewer: 2b191355afbca1b93ba0438bf798d126dcb3172f -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers. The notes below are not blocking.

Head `2b191355a`, trial-merged with `origin/main` at `33685374f` (clean merge). All runs are local (no `pr-test.yml`).

### What looks good
- Part 2 drops only suites that have no ignored test. The heavy step runs `--ignored` only (`xtask/src/plan.rs:260`). Thus a dropped suite loses no release-mode coverage of a normal test. The release `--no-run` build still names each crate with `-p`, so the release build is the same.
- Each guard fails to the safe side: a walk error, a missing module file, an unreadable file, `include!`, `#[path`, `#[cfg_attr(.., path = ..)]`, and a `mod` token that the line scan does not read.
- Part 1 falls back to the whole suite when it is not sure: no merge-base text (a new or renamed file), `main.rs`, `pub`/`pub(..)`, macros (now or at the base), cfg-gated files, two submodules.
- The filter `<sub>::` has the trailing `::`, so `cases::` does not select `cases_extra::`. A substring hit such as `other::cases::x` only runs more tests. A nested module (`<sub>::inner::`) is inside the prefix.
- The changed pin `quick_checks_old_and_new_hunk_sides_without_widening_in_test_edits` is correct. Its first case deletes a private helper of `cases` that only `cases` uses, and the base text has no `pub`. `cases::` covers all affected tests.

### Results (merged tree, local)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -j 6 -p xtask -- --test-threads=6`, unit tests | 311 passed |
| integration binaries (11) | all pass: catalog 4, docs_images 4, example_line_endings 3, lane_verdict 0, merge_ready_skill 3, merge_review 0, post_merge_concurrency 2, post_merge_report 1, post_merge_stall 1, release_site_tests 3, review_artifacts 3 |
| `cargo clippy -j 6 -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Note: my first run of `catalog` stopped with exit 143. My own 590 s `timeout` wrapper stopped its inner `camcraft-cli` build. The binary then ran alone with no wrapper: 4 passed.

### Independent check of part 2
I did not use the author's script.
- `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run` with the xtask of `origin/main`: 273 heavy steps. With the merged xtask: 99. 174 steps are dropped, 0 are added, and all other steps are the same (1458 lines to 1284 lines, and the difference is only the dropped heavy steps).
- The `lib`, `bins` and `doc` heavy steps of `kernel`, `motion` and `app` do not change.
- For each dropped step, my resolver read the entry file, each `mod x;` (to `x.rs` or `x/mod.rs`, recursively), each `#[path]` and `include!`. It also read all files under `tests/common/`, each directory that a `mod` names, and the whole directory of a directory suite. The result: 174 dropped steps, 0 unresolved, **0 with `ignore` (any case) in a `.rs` file**.
- 16 steps had a hit only in a `.cps` post file (`fanuc.cps`, `tormach-lathe.cps`) that the test reads with `include_str!`. That is post-processor text, not Rust, and it cannot declare a test.
- Reverse check: `grep -rln "#\[ignore" crates/*/tests crates/*/src` gives 49 files. Each test file and each lib of a heavy crate keeps its heavy step in the merged plan: **0 lost**. A second walk over all 856 binaries of the heavy crates gives the same result: 0 lost. No macro in `crates/*/src` emits `#[ignore]`. `shared_face_bodies_finish` (a macro with an ignored test) keeps its step.

### Heavy lanes
`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run`: the diff reaches no heavy lane (0 steps).

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions and notes (not blocking)
1. Part 1, trait impls. `quick_subs::filter` (`xtask/src/quick_subs.rs:26`) treats a submodule with no `pub` as private. But an `impl SomeTrait for SomeType` in a private submodule is visible everywhere. A change to such an impl can change a test in a different submodule, and `<sub>::` does not run that test. On main now, no private submodule of a directory suite has an `impl .. for`, so no case exists today. Recommended: add `impl\b[^{;]*\bfor\b` to the `shared` regex.
2. Part 1, attribute before `pub`. The regex `(?m)^\s*pub\b` does not find `#[allow(dead_code)] pub fn x()` on one line. rustfmt normally moves the attribute to its own line, so the risk is small. A count of `\bpub\b` on `braces::code` output would close this.
3. The batch tier (post-merge) still runs each whole suite, so a quick-tier miss from 1 or 2 is found after the merge. It is not lost.
4. `braces::code` has no direct unit test. Only `a_clean_flat_suite_with_a_clean_module_gets_no_heavy_step` tests it (a `mod` in a comment and in a string). An error that blanks real code (for example `cr"..."` read as a normal string) hides `mod` tokens. That makes the guard weaker, not stronger. Recommended: a small table test with raw strings `r#"..."#`, nested `/* /* */ */`, `'"'`, `'\''`, lifetimes `'a` and `b"..."`. I read the lexer for these cases and found no error that hides code.
5. In `quick_checks_old_and_new_hunk_sides_without_widening_in_test_edits`, the loop variable `whole` now means "outside the test fns". A new name would make this clear.

### Process
- The body has `Process change: yes`, `Changelog: none` and `Fixes #3706`. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is not changed.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/3706-xtask-submodule-filter.md` is present.
- Line counts: `quick.rs` 362, `plan.rs` 325, `suites.rs` 204, `braces.rs` 99, `quick_subs.rs` 79, `quick_describe.rs` 59, `directory_selection_tests.rs` 189, `directory_edges_tests.rs` 169. All are under 400.

The PR stays a draft as its author set it. A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
